comment.narrative: 4.4.1Feasibility studies developed for rice straw and husk and carbon credit scheme

An initial study has been conducted on rice byproducts and carbon credits in Indonesia. As observed the small rice millers involved in the project have identified the byproducts except straw as potential additional income for example husk ash and bran being utilised by the poultry industries for feeds or other uses. Regardng the carbon credit on 26 September 2023 the government officially launched the Indonesian Carbon Exchange facilitated by the Indonesian Stock Exchange BEI under the authorisation of the Financial Services Authority. Feasibility study on a new business model for byproducts and on the sale of carbon credits within the rice sector in Indonesia.will be conduct on 2024.

title.narrative: 1.GHG emissions reductions attributed to rice production in the 5 project districts.

description.narrative: 1.GHG emissions reductions attributed to rice production in the 5 project districts.

comment.narrative: 1.Baseline to be determined via baseline study at project start.
1.GHG emissions from rice production reduced by 15 for project participants across 5 project districts.

The exact value is not available yet. The baseline study on GHG emission at the smallrice millers is available. The base line study shows that 85 of the GHG emission is from the diesel fuels uses by the smallrice millers.On 2023 the project conducted technical assistance to 150 smallrice millers to improve the machine configuration which help reduce the use of diesel fuels. There are 26 smallrice millers have been migrated to electricity as energy source to run the operation with estimation GHG reduction up to 138. On 2024 the project will calculate the GHG reduction at the rice millers across 5 project districts.
